=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each
(AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether
each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Overall assessment

**Do not accept the Seller’s package as drafted.** It combines broad disclosure and buyer-knowledge exclusions with a relatively narrow warranty remedy, while leaving important completion risks unresolved. The combined effect matters more than any individual cap: the Seller could disclose a problem, exclude a warranty claim and still leave Wattlebridge funding or remedying it after Completion.

Our baseline remains **100% of Paperbark Analytics for AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free, under NSW law**. The Seller’s descriptions of matters as “addressed”, “ordinary course” or “settled” are negotiating positions—not evidence or Buyer agreement.

This review is based on the supplied update and disclosure letter, not the underlying SPA or DD documents. Those documents must be checked before settling drafting or approving Completion.

## 1. Liability regime: prevent general limits from swallowing specific protections

### All-Claims limitations — reject

Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5, together with the proposed default in clauses 12.3/13, could extend warranty limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions to **every kind of claim**.

That could undermine claims for unpaid purchase-price adjustments, breach of completion obligations, historic tax, specific indemnities and title defects—not just general warranties.

**Push back:**
- Apply the general warranty regime only to clearly defined general warranty claims.
- Give tax, fundamental warranties and specific indemnities their own express regimes.
- Preserve enforcement of payment obligations, debt discharge, price adjustments and other contractual undertakings.
- Include clear priority language so specific protections override inconsistent general limitations.
- Preserve remedies for fraud and fraudulent concealment, and rights that cannot lawfully be excluded. Review any exclusion of statutory misleading-conduct remedies rather than assuming boilerplate non-reliance language is acceptable or effective.

### General cap, thresholds and timing — negotiate as a package

The proposed **AUD 4.8 million cap** is 20% of the price. It is not inherently impermissible, but is seller-friendly alongside:
- a AUD 25,000 de minimis;
- a **deductible**, not tipping, AUD 250,000 basket;
- an 18-month notification period; and
- broad disclosure and knowledge exclusions.

For example, AUD 300,000 of qualifying aggregate claims would yield only AUD 50,000 before other limitations.

**Push back:**
- Seek a higher general cap, supported by the diligence risk and available recovery security.
- Seek a lower de minimis and basket, preferably a tipping basket.
- Aggregate related claims arising from the same facts so fragmentation does not defeat recovery.
- Seek at least 24 months for general warranties, covering two reporting cycles where practicable.
- Ensure timely notified claims survive expiry; avoid unduly technical notice requirements or a short deadline to commence proceedings.

Any compromise must be assessed against the final exclusions, security and specific protections—not the cap alone.

### Fundamental/title warranties — separate treatment

“Administrative simplicity” does not justify limiting title and capacity claims to 20% or 18 months. Wattlebridge is paying for ownership of all shares, not merely a limited claim if that ownership fails.

Seek a separate cap of **at least the purchase price**, no de minimis or basket, and a substantially longer claim period appropriate to fundamental obligations. The precise survival and enforcement drafting should be checked against applicable limitation rules.

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge: stop diligence becoming a blanket waiver

The general disclosure of everything “contained or referred to” in the data room and public records is too broad. Referenced material may not even have been provided. Clause 8.3 goes further by excluding matters merely **discoverable** by Wattlebridge or its advisers.

Together, these provisions could convert access to information into assumed knowledge and risk acceptance.

**Push back:**
- Require **fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter**, linked to relevant warranties.
- Reject wholesale deemed disclosure of the data room and public registers.
- Freeze and retain an agreed, indexed copy of any disclosure materials accepted.
- Delete constructive or discoverable knowledge and imputed knowledge of all advisers.
- Prefer no Buyer-knowledge exclusion; if necessary, limit it to actual conscious knowledge of specified individuals.
- State expressly that disclosure or knowledge does not qualify agreed indemnities, conditions, price adjustments or other specifically allocated risks.

The disclosure letter itself acknowledges major evidentiary gaps. **Disclosure is not remediation, consent or an agreement that Wattlebridge bears the risk.**

## 3. Bluefen: make effective consent a genuine completion condition

Bluefen represents approximately **AUD 3.6 million, or 30%, of FY26 revenue**. Its consent is therefore commercially significant.

The letter says neither final written consent nor evidence of satisfaction of associated conditions is included. The Seller’s proposal to deem the condition satisfied on delivery of written consent could overlook clause 11.3 requirements, conditional consent, price concessions or termination rights.

**Require:**
- Review of the complete clauses 11.2 and 11.3.
- Effective consent covering the actual transaction, with all associated conditions satisfied.
- No materially adverse amendment, fee or concession without Buyer approval.
- A completion condition waivable only by Wattlebridge, with an appropriate long-stop date and termination right.

Reasonable endeavours may regulate the Seller’s efforts; they are **not a substitute for the required outcome**.

## 4. Riverlark: discharge at Completion, not afterwards

Leaving approximately **AUD 3.2 million** outstanding and providing a release after Completion conflicts with the debt-free acquisition and exposes the acquired business to continuing lender rights.

**Require:**
- A current payout letter covering principal, interest, fees and break costs.
- Direct repayment through the completion funds flow.
- Binding discharge/release arrangements effective at Completion, covering all relevant security and guarantees.
- Appropriate evidence and arrangements for subsequent registry updates.
- Resolution of the facility’s change-control requirements so no intervening default arises.

Reconcile the debt treatment with the price mechanism. The repayment must reduce the amount otherwise payable to the Seller where required by the agreed debt-free/cash-free mechanics—not become an additional Buyer cost above AUD 24 million. Avoid double counting any deduction and repayment.

## 5. Completion bonuses: recognise the full transaction cost

The **AUD 420,000** bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, so they should not automatically be described as presently accrued liabilities. However, their omission from the funds flow is a material economic gap.

Calling them “a matter for the Seller” does not protect Wattlebridge if Paperbark must pay them after Completion.

**Require:**
- Confirmation of the obligor, payment dates and all vesting conditions.
- Calculation of applicable employer on-costs, including payroll tax and superannuation where applicable, and correct withholding arrangements.
- Express treatment as Seller transaction expenses, debt-like items or a specific price deduction, as appropriate under the agreed mechanism.
- Seller funding or a secured reimbursement obligation where payment occurs after Completion.

Ensure the cost is captured once, without duplicating working-capital or debt adjustments.

## 6. Ironquay IP: protect ownership, not just the unpaid fee

The materials indicate that transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of **every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but this is not conclusive proof of non-payment. Equally, there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.

An indemnity restricted to the SOW3 payment may leave Wattlebridge exposed to loss of rights, infringement allegations, remediation costs and business disruption.

**Require:**
- Reconciliation of all SOW3 fees and bank-supported payment evidence.
- Review of the agreement and IP chain of title, including relevant subcontractor rights.
- A binding confirmatory assignment or other sufficient evidence that Paperbark owns or has the required rights.
- Completion deliverables where the materials are material to the business.
- A broader specific indemnity covering the identified ownership/use risk and resulting losses, with separate limits and survival.

Do not let the disclosure neutralise that indemnity.

## 7. Export/privacy incident: investigate and allocate the unresolved risk

The current evidence establishes an unintended external delivery of a download link, potentially involving approximately **1,240 records**. It does **not** establish unauthorised access, a notifiable breach or a loss amount. Conversely, a preliminary investigation cannot support the Seller’s assurance that the matter is immaterial.

**Require:**
- Preservation and review of access logs, link permissions, expiry/revocation and containment evidence.
- Confirmation of the actual dataset, recipients and any access or onward disclosure.
- Assessment of applicable privacy, contractual and notification obligations.
- Buyer oversight of material investigation and remediation decisions, without delaying legally required action.
- Updated disclosure and warranties through Completion.
- A specific allocation of pre-Completion incident liabilities, supported by an indemnity and, if justified, retention/security.

Consider a completion condition if investigation identifies material unresolved exposure; do not assume one is necessary solely from the present facts.

## 8. Supplier renewals: assess substance and timing

Three related renewals total **AUD 330,000**. The record does not establish that they are ordinary-course, unavoidable or properly chargeable to the post-Completion business.

Review DD-008 and DD-011 together for execution dates, service periods, cancellation rights, commercial need and accounting treatment.

**Push back:** prohibit material new commitments without Buyer consent pending Completion. Determine whether these are genuine future operating expenses, existing liabilities, prepayments or exceptional Seller-period commitments before deciding their price treatment. They should neither be automatically deducted nor automatically accepted.

## 9. Tax and general IP protections are not “settled”

The Seller’s statement does not establish agreement.

- **Tax:** seek a dedicated covenant/indemnity for pre-Completion tax liabilities, with appropriate exclusions against double recovery, tax claim procedures and survival aligned to relevant assessment periods. Do not apply the general basket or 18-month limit.
- **IP:** retain meaningful warranties addressing ownership, licences, infringement and relevant third-party/open-source dependencies. Consider enhanced survival and recovery limits given the business’s nature. General IP warranties do not replace the Ironquay-specific protection.

## 10. Title, lease and Mossvale: verify without inventing consent requirements

- **Title:** DD-012 is relevant evidence, not complete verification. Check issued capital, beneficial ownership, encumbrances, options and other rights, constitutional restrictions, and valid transfer/registration deliverables.
- **Office lease:** the disclosed obligation is notification, not landlord consent. Obtain the full clause and ensure compliant notice; do not invent a consent condition.
- **Mossvale:** an assignment restriction does not, by itself, require consent to a share sale. Check for separate change-control or deemed-assignment wording before determining requirements.

## Recommended negotiating priorities

1. **Completion protections:** effective Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment/releases and satisfactory resolution of material Ironquay ownership issues.
2. **Price integrity:** reconcile debt, bonuses and on-costs, and supplier commitments in one auditable funds-flow and adjustment schedule.
3. **Preserve recourse:** reject all-Claims limitations and blanket disclosure/knowledge exclusions; separate title, tax and specific indemnity regimes.
4. **Resolve uncertainty:** complete the incident investigation and underlying document review before accepting the Seller’s characterisations.
5. **Secure recovery:** assess Seller covenant strength and seek an appropriate retention, escrow or guarantee. A favourable indemnity is worth little without recoverable funds.

**Bottom line:** known risks should be cured, priced or expressly indemnified—not merely disclosed and then excluded from recovery.
